_note: 60-second sprint questions. For study only, not clinical guidance. 'answer' is the zero-based index of the correct option. 'category' must match a name in assets/catalog.js.

questions.stem: Which mechanism lowers the partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood itself, not only the haemoglobin carrying it?
questions.why: Hypoventilation lowers PaO₂ and raises PaCO₂ because less gas reaches the alveoli. Anaemia and low output reduce content with a normal PaO₂.

questions.stem: Standard pulse oximetry can read falsely normal in which situation?
questions.why: Carboxyhaemoglobin is read as oxyhaemoglobin by a two-wavelength oximeter, so SpO₂ can look normal while oxygen delivery is poor.

questions.stem: In a young, fit adult who is losing blood, which sign usually changes first?
questions.why: Compensated shock raises heart rate and tightens vessels, keeping pressure normal until late. Tachycardia is the early sign.

questions.stem: Which temperature is conventionally used to define fever in adults?
questions.why: 38.0 °C is the usual threshold. 37.5 °C is low-grade, and 39.0 °C is a high fever rather than the definition.

questions.stem: Kussmaul breathing is best described as which pattern?
questions.why: Deep, rapid, laboured breathing is respiratory compensation for metabolic acidosis, as in diabetic ketoacidosis.
